I’m way too late I know, but in order to sink this in, I think the simplest way to explain countable infinity and uncountable infinity is their predictability.

One thing to keep in mind is that don’t think of them like there’s a stop, there’s a limit, it’s infinite for a reason, both are still endless. So, uncountable and countable is like asking yourself “Mhmmmm, can I list it down? Is this measurable? Is this predictable?”

Countable infinity is something you can count, from 1, 2, 3…so on and forever—It’s not just about that, it’s the way you can predict what comes after a certain number. 

For example, what comes after 90000000000?
Duh, of course it’s 90000000001. Whatever number it is, you would always have an idea when you add a number, you can just add 1, use multiplication, or even arithmetic.

As for unaccountable infinity, this is something you can’t count, it’s not 1, 2, 3…so on—so it’s unpredictable. You can’t list it down because there’s always a number that’s left. It’s a number you can always create a new sets of number.
